answer: Sybil resistance here works through a per-identity ledger that carries forward, like a garden that only rewards seed actually planted: each wallet must post a stake and hold a unique attestation link before mining output unlocks. A single operator spinning up many keys gains nothing, because each clone would need its own funded escrow and independent attestations, a plume of aliases that costs real capital every time. The mirror effect is symmetric: rewards scale with verified history per key, never with key count, so faking one hundred identities multiplies cost, not income.
